profile.address: Lookout Drive, Garland, Dallas County, Texas, 75082
profile.reading: This point is mapped to Lookout Drive in Garland, TX, without a house number, placing it somewhere on NTT's real Dallas-area data center campus. NTT's own site confirms two buildings by street address on Lookout Drive: TX1 at 2008 Lookout Dr (230,000 square feet, 16 megawatts of critical IT load, with SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, NIST 800-53 High, and HIPAA compliance attestations) and TX4 at 2060 Lookout Dr (127,000 square feet, 36 megawatts, part of a 124-megawatt campus, stated as becoming available from June 2026). Data center directory Baxtel additionally lists TX2 at 2108 Lookout Dr and TX3 at 2080 Lookout Dr, both roughly 229,500 square feet and operational since 2024, though MW figures for TX2 and TX3 are not disclosed in that secondary source. Because this specific mapped point lacks a house number, this entry cannot confirm which of NTT's four Lookout Drive buildings it corresponds to, and does not guess; it is presented here as part of the shared Garland, TX data center campus rather than assigned false building-specific figures. RagingWire (NTT's US brand) announced the campus in 2022 as a planned 1-million-square-foot, 80-megawatt-plus development, since expanded further per the individual building figures above. Data Center Frontier toured TX1 and reports the Garland campus was established in 2016 on the former RagingWire site and has been operational since 2017, with the 42-acre megacampus ultimately planned to hold over one million square feet and 144 megawatts of critical IT load at full buildout. NTT announced a 50 million dollar fit out of the TX2 and TX3 buildings in June 2023, adding nearly 300,000 square feet of data vault and office space with each building rated at 36 megawatts, using air cooled chillers with fan coil wall designs distinct from TX1s original cooling configuration. A further 42 million dollar, 236,000 square foot fourth building was reported under construction from September 2025 through an expected April 2026 completion, expanding the 47 acre site. Cushman and Wakefield market data cited alongside that expansion put existing Dallas-Fort Worth data center capacity at 4.5 million square feet by the end of 2023 with only 178,000 square feet available for lease, reflecting the tight vacancy driving continued campus growth at this site.

profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 93 (NTT Dallas cluster, further attempt): operators own overview page confirms Dallas TX1 and TX4 buildings and a 124 MW planned campus but no addresses, dedicated pages 404. Two of four rows geocoded to Lookout Dr, Garland, TX, assessed as likely residential rather than the actual campus and not applied, alongside an unconfirmed Telecom Parkway alternate. research_status upgraded from exhausted to complete for all four rows, no address applied to any.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to NTT, part of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation, one of the largest telecommunications and IT services groups in the world, headquartered in Tokyo, Japan. NTT operates a global data center business, NTT Global Data Centers, under NTT DATA, Inc. The operators own about us page, fetched this session, states NTT DATA is a top 10 global IT services provider with about 30 billion dollars in annual revenue, operations across 33 countries, and about 3 billion dollars in annual research and development investment, headquartered at the Toyosu Center Building, 3-3-3 Toyosu, Koto-ku, Tokyo 135-6033, Japan, though these figures describe the wider NTT DATA organization rather than the data center division specifically, and no data center division formation or acquisition date was found on the pages fetched this session. A previously confirmed, specific data center acquisition remains NTT Communications purchase of an 86.7 percent stake in e-shelter, described as Germany top data center operator, completed around June 23, 2015, though that acquisition is not directly connected to this United States facility. This session reached the operators own services.global.ntt data center locations pages directly and successfully. An earlier sessions attempts to reach the ragingwire.com domain had failed and found no corresponding Wikipedia article, a negative finding this session did not need to repeat. The operators own current Dallas area locations overview page, fetched this session, names two buildings, Dallas TX1 Data Center and Dallas TX4 Data Center, and states a planned 124 MW IT load once the campus is fully built out, but gives no street address for either. Dedicated TX1 and TX4 facility pages, guessed from the naming pattern used successfully elsewhere for this operator, both returned 404. Reverse geocoding two of this four row clusters own coordinates through a third party service returned addresses on Lookout Dr in Garland, TX, at 0.9 confidence each, though at wider distances than typical for a confident match, and the tightly spaced, small increment numbering seen among the candidate and nearby alternate addresses on that street, for example 1788, 1792, 1796, 1800, and 1908, reads as consistent with an ordinary residential subdivision rather than a data center campus. One geocode response also surfaced an unconfirmed alternate candidate, 7200 Telecom Parkway in nearby Richardson, TX, a street name more thematically consistent with a telecom or data facility, but this was not independently confirmed by a second geocode point or any other source. Given the residential character of the primary candidate street and the lack of a confirming second source for either candidate, this session does not apply an address to any row in this four row cluster.

reading.body:
NTT operates a planned 124 MW campus in the Dallas area, confirmed by the operator's own overview page as two buildings, Dallas TX1 and Dallas TX4, but the operator has not published a street address. The campus location in Dallas County cannot be verified to street precision from available sources. If built to spec, this campus would rank 19th among Texas facilities with published power capacity, though 133 mapped facilities in the state publish no capacity figure.

At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 124 MW of IT load would support roughly 3,100 racks. The published capacity figure suggests a major expansion of NTT's regional presence, representing about 27 percent of the 468 MW of published data center capacity across Texas. This campus would be the largest AI-scale facility confirmed in the state if completed as planned.

The operator is NTT Global Data Centers, part of NTT DATA, a top 10 global IT services provider headquartered in Tokyo. No tenant names, service certifications, grid interconnection details, or construction timeline have been published for this campus.
